head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1438 — High: `if w.startswith("/."): continue` is unconditional, so any absolute path written with a `/./` or `/../` prefix (`cat /./home/operator/secret`, `cat /../root/.ssh/id_rsa`) is never a candidate, although `outside()` would normpath it to an outside path. The comment's rationale ("no Linux root holds dot-dirs") is wrong for `.`/`..`; the quoted-tail case it targets is already covered by the 1.2.5 glue rule. Normalise first, or drop the rule.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1377 — High: the HEREDOC regex consumes `[^\n]*` after the delimiter, so the rest of the opening line is stripped along with the body and never scanned: `cat <<EOF && cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa` or `cat <<EOF > /home/operator/out` is no longer a hit (it was in 1.2.0). Strip only from the first newline onward.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1412 — High: strip_heredocs treats every heredoc body as "written data", but a heredoc fed to an interpreter (`python3 - <<'PY'\nopen('/root/.ssh/id_rsa')…`, `bash <<EOF`) is executed code. Outside reads through that very common pattern now escape contamination detection. Limit the stripping to heredocs redirected into a file (cat > f <<, tee f <<).
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1365 — High: after_closing_quote counts any quote preceded by a non-space as "closing". So `''/home/operator/secret`, `"/home"/operator/secret` (the one-component `/home` is skipped by in_quotes at :1444, the tail by :1442) and, in host mode, `"$HOME"/.ssh/id_rsa` / `"${HOME}"/.aws/credentials` (HOME_WORD needs `$HOME/` with no quote between) all pass as clean.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1374 — Medium: in_quotes counts every `'` and `"` before the position and ignores escapes, nesting and command boundaries. One apostrophe earlier in the command (`git commit -m "it's done"; ls /root`) puts a later sensitive one-component word such as /root "inside a literal", so it is skipped.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1432 — Medium: `"=" in w` drops the whole word, but ABS_WORD's class includes `=` and `,`, so a real path with a glued suffix (`cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa,x=1`, `/home/operator/a=b`) is no longer a candidate. "No path component carries =" is false on Linux. Only the regex/key=value shape should be skipped.

content.text: Thirteen findings are written so far. The review of the report script is still running, and I'll add its findings and the verdict once it finishes.

I found two real defects in the statistics, both affecting decisions, plus a few minor ones. The predicate order, interval computation, signs and pairing all check out. I read the files only; nothing was run.

**What checks out.** The predicate order in `decide()` (lines 588–615) matches the YAML: degradation guard, investigate, keep, inconclusive, remove, simplify. The strict and inclusive comparisons use `r9` correctly. The percentile function (lines 180–189) is numpy-linear with q=0.05/0.95. The 90% MDE z-values are right. d is arm − A1 for components, a1 − a0 for H1 (lo > 0) and a4 − a1 for A4 (hi < 0). Pairwise drops and reruns that supersede an excluded row work as the header says. Every division is guarded (lines 489, 578, 203). I also checked the expected values in AR-1 to AR-11 and AR-21 by hand: they follow from the generated rows.

**Findings**

1. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:471-483, 541-546` — **Medium-High** (confidence high on the facts, medium on intent). The per-defect "ids" path never runs on real rows, so every real catch-rate decision rests on artificially narrow intervals.
   - The report reads `defects_missed` or `recall.missed` from the row.
   - `ablation-grade.sh:1319` does write `recall.missed`, but `ablation-row.sh` (lines 339–375) only copies `defects_seeded`, `defects_caught`, `defect_catch_rate` and `flags` into the row.
   - So every real review-catch comparison takes the `"rate"` fallback: the task's diff is copied once per defect (8 copies for rc-01).
   - Those copies are then resampled as if independent, which inflates `n` (and shrinks the MDE as 1/sqrt(n)). The decision interval and MDE come out much narrower than the data supports, so Keep/Investigate on `defect_catch_rate` can fire on what is really task-level noise.
   - The tests hide this. AR-7 passes only because `gen-fixtures.py:77-78` plants `defects_missed`, a field real rows never carry. AR-20 ("planted rows hold the real row shape") doesn't catch it because `--validate` accepts extra fields.

2. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:202-204, 637, 643` — **Medium** (confidence high). The power cut skips exactly the weakest samples.
   - With n == 1, `mde()` returns None and line 637 keeps only `p["mde"] is not None`, so a Remove or Simplify from a single paired task is never turned into Inconclusive-by-power.
   - With n == 1, `bootstrap()` also returns lo = hi = d. One task can therefore yield a final Investigate (d > 0) or Keep (d < −0.03) with a zero-width "90% interval". This bites with `--partial` and with arms that have few tasks.

3. `head/evals/tests/ablation-report.bats:311` — **Low** (confidence high). This check always passes. `grep -qF 'degradation guard first'` matches fixed Method text written into every report (`ablation-report.py:1004-1005`, "...9 decimals, the degradation guard first (excluded share..."). The decision rule string reads "degradation guard, evaluated first", which doesn't match. The `.label` check on line 310 is the only real assertion in AR-22.

4. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:300-302` — **Low** (confidence high). If one run_id appears three times, the first duplicate entry records `kept` as line 2, but line 2 is then dropped too. Line 921 prints "the row at <kept> is used" for a row that isn't used.

5. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:452-453 with 486-491, 744` — **Low** (confidence medium). The sensitivity analysis excludes cap failures, which also adds them to the excluded share. An arm with many cap failures (a likely real effect of removing a component) then shows Inconclusive-by-degradation in the sensitivity table instead of an actual sensitivity outcome. No decision reads it, but it can make the figure uninformative.

6. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:486-491` — **Low** (confidence low: the spec is ambiguous). The share counts only the arm's own cells. A1 is never decided, so heavy exclusions on the control side are never guarded: if 30% of A1's cells are contaminated, every arm loses those pairs and none trips the 0.25 guard. The YAML's "the arm's excluded share" can be read either way.

7. `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:459-460` — **Low** (latent; confidence high). `_classify` writes `_valid`/`_reason` into row dicts that the main and sensitivity analyses share. The sensitivity pass overwrites cap-failure rows' `_valid` to False. It's harmless today because main computes cell validity in `__init__` (lines 397–407) before the sensitivity analysis is built. Any later read of `row["_valid"]` from main would get the sensitivity value.

Minor and not a correctness issue: AR-12 (`bats:179-188`) copies the code's own rules-block extraction logic (lines 252–261), so it can't catch a bug in that logic.
